svg.title: How rank 7 admits its weights
svg.desc: A threshold of model authorities signs a manifest with rank-ordered weight roots. Assembly provisioning binds physical device identities and permitted ranks. Rank 7 verifies the manifest, finds its own provisioned rank and establishes a fresh run with the group. Its page checker authenticates local HBM data against its assigned root before delivering weights to compute.

g.text: Boot binds the model to an authorized group. During inference, every weight page must match the admitted commitment.
Sign the model identifier, numerical profile
Pins the roster of device public keys
Prove possession of their device keys
Verify the signature threshold using fixed
authority keys. Accept an implemented profile.
Match my provisioned identity to the roster.
Select the shard root assigned to rank 7.
Agree on the model, group and fresh run ID.
Derive session keys with authenticated peers.
Persistent trust anchors include the authority keys, the roster commitment and this die’s protected private identity.
Check its directory entry, index and bytes.
A mismatch blocks delivery to arithmetic and faults the run.
In the fixed-model version (F-AWIC), all dies can pin one common model-manifest digest. That manifest commits to every rank’s shard.
A signed-update AWIC (S-AWIC) can admit a new authorized manifest at a fresh boot. Weight confidentiality also requires encryption and key provision.
